## 1. Wrong controlled phase

Change exactly D10.body.j and M10.body.j from 1 to 2. Preserve k=2, target=123,
both interfaces, all P/E rows and all other D/M rows. D14 still positively
controls D13, whose tensor D12 contains the changed D10 phase. Therefore the
actual controlled angle changes from pi/2 to pi.

`Artifact.angleValid` admits 2 < 2^2. `Rule.bodies` for phase requires equal
actual/logical j and k, with no premises; P10 already has the plain empty
witness and E7 on both endpoints. Hence there is no proof parameter or encoding
to rewrite. Own-artifact acceptance is predicted, not observed. The fixed
Fourier request should reject because `Gradient.shape` requires numerator=1
at the actual phase node. Preserve actual diagnostics; do not claim that the
public `contract` code identifies the internal predicate uniquely.

## 2. Cancelled real reversal

Change exactly the newly added final post-route D.body.permutation.axes and
its associated M.body.permutation.axes from `[0,1]` to `[1,0]`. Obtain the D/M
indices from the frozen adapter association and verify their P association;
do not assume they are equal or reuse predicted ordinal 33 silently. Preserve

map, P rule/premises/witness/endpoints, identity E rows and every original row.

This is an extra real positional reversal which cancels the existing one,
not deletion of the original reversal. D29 remains sequence `[26,27,28]`:
D26 takes position 0; D27 puts it at position 1; D28 renames labels with the
identity positional map. D30 is also an identity positional map although its
output label array is `[1,0]`. Label array order alone is not a reversal.

`Ports.coordinates` uses declared positions without sorting labels, so the
changed two-axis permutation is a valid same-`Bits<2>` route. `Rule.bodies`
compares the equal D/M maps; identity boundary encodings need no change.
No row becomes unreachable, unlike replacing D29 and forgetting to compact
the old subgraph. Own-artifact acceptance is predicted. `Wiring.compose`
computes the actual suffix: reverse followed by reverse becomes `[0,1]`, so
`FourierRoot.routes` should reject the frozen request which requires `[1,0]`.

## 3. Actual H leaf replaced by X

Target original D3, the high-bit H leaf under closed H wrapper D5=[D3,D4].
Its embedded original QIRF2 program is 415 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256
`a9b652473b8773393a02421a9d03fba1ddd2c13a1a2be1b30e53b5b3eef4d67e`.
The exact substring `"gate":"h"` occurs once. Replace only that substring
with `"gate":"x"`, requiring count==1 before replacement. Parse both strings
as data afterward and assert that the only semantic JSON delta is
programs[0].operations[0].gate h->x. Retain every unrelated embedded byte,
including the final newline. The gate remains input125/output126 on wire1;
QIRF sources/evidence stay empty, root remains 0, declared effect is unitary,
and the complete Bit->Bit root interface remains unchanged.

Change only M3.body.description.entries to the independently specified
row-major X matrix `[0,1,1,0]`, preserving its format/version/domain/rows/cols.
Encode zero as four coefficients `(numerator="0", denominator_bits=0)`;
encode one as `[("1",0),("0",0),("0",0),("0",0)]`. This uses the existing
`zeta8-dyadic-v1` exact scalar representation, with no floating approximations.
The original M3 description is 737 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256
`eab90807ea4a9f2a2f4934f21473d534090cd21827345cbc1d953a03d39dcf2a`.
Preserve D3/M3 interfaces, P3 finite rule and plain witness, E3->E4, rename D4,
low-bit H D16/M16 and all other rows. Record the new program/description hashes
and a field-delta map when a generator is later authorized.

`Protocol.Raw.gate` already decodes x. `Semantics.RawTrace.gate` interprets it
as monomial `[1,0]` with phases `[0,0]`; exact finite reconstruction compares
its full matrix with M3's proposed X. This is a changed opaque finite provider
implementation and its own proposed meaning, not a new primitive or source
provider, nor an H annotation check. The retained source still imports actual
`std::quantum::h`; this artifact mutant makes no source-preservation claim.
Fresh own inspection should accept X. The Fourier shape still has the same
two-child leaf/rename wrapper and interfaces, so its returned H obligation

against their own meanings and checks those original bytes again against
